content.value: Runes are equipment modifiers created through the Runic Altar or generated on mob equipment. A rune has a prefix or suffix position, a tier, a rolled value, a rune-level requirement for random crafting, a selection weight, and a compatibility group.
Three Ways to Obtain a Rune

Random rune: ordinary Runic Tomes choose from the item's compatible random pool. The weapon and armour catalog pages list only these genuinely random-rollable affixes.
Targeted rune: Elemental, Haste, and Body tomes guarantee one named family instead of selecting randomly. Some targeted results also exist in the random pool, while special Extra Damage and Physical Taken as Void modifiers are targeted-only.
Artificial rune: an Artificial Tome reserves one prefix or suffix on a Rare item, then the Artificial Altar lets you choose from up to three compatible options.

Prefix and suffix capacity is separate. Magic equipment can hold one prefix and one suffix; Rare equipment can hold three of each. A random tome tries a random side first and then the other side if the first cannot accept a legal result. A rune consumes one slot even when it grants several component values.

Related versions of a stat share a group ID. An item cannot hold two runes from the same group even when their internal IDs differ. Hybrid runes roll several components together but consume only their own single affix position.

Local flat physical damage, armour, evasion, and Energy Shield are merged with the item's base. Local percentage then scales base + flat. These values are baked into the item's attribute component so they are not added a second time as global stats.

Global runes contribute to the character or attack calculation: attributes, life, mana, resistance, global critical chance, elemental damage, ailment chance/magnitude, leech, projectile behaviour, regeneration, and similar bonuses. Conditional wording only applies while its named condition is true.

The mace, trident, turtle helmet, and Elytra are Unique and reject every Runic Altar operation. Horse armour, wolf armour, axes, pickaxes, shovels, and hoes also cannot receive affixes. Unique-only internal modifiers are intentionally omitted from the rune catalogs.

Read Using the Runic Altar before spending a tome. Item rarity, open prefix/suffix capacity, duplicate groups, equipment compatibility, and the tome's own input-rarity rule must all allow the operation.
